data.summary: The paper woman opens a separate teal umbrella and folded drops bounce from it. The canopy stays upright above her rather than tilting toward a flower, and drops continue striking the uncovered cream flowers. The final push-in also clips the left canopy edge.

observations.text: One recognizable woman in folded-paper clothing looks up at blue paper rain, slides a hand along the umbrella shaft and opens the teal canopy. Her braids, skirt and leaf cape remain recognizable.

The umbrella is held over her head as rain contacts and tumbles off its facets. She looks toward the right-side flowers, but the umbrella does not move to shelter them; several drops continue onto flower heads.

She returns her gaze toward camera while holding the shaft with two distinct hands. The flower remains uncovered, including a drop on a cream flower at the ending. The closer view cuts the canopy at the left boundary; canopy and leaf cape do not merge.
